newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court considers claim in Hernu "spying" case.
newsitem.headline: French court considers claim in Hernu "spying" case.

text.p: A French court agreed on Wednesday to consider a claim for damages by the sons of the late Socialist defence minister Charles Hernu against the weekly L'Express, which accused him of spying for the communist bloc.
Jean-Michel, Jean-Charles and Patrice Hernu accused L'Express of backing up its allegations with falsified documents and demanded 30 million francs ($5.5 million) in damages.
The court said it would study the claim, but would rule only after a criminal court gives its verdict on charges of forgery and swindling which Hernu's family have brought against the weekly.

L'Express caused a political storm when it published documents in October and January purporting to show that Hernu, under the codename "Andre", had been a Soviet, Romanian and Bulgarian agent in the 1950s and 1960s.
Hernu, defence minister from 1981 to 1985, died in 1990.
His sons say the documents may be fake, and that even if genuine, they were not honestly and accurately translated.
"We are therefore completely satisfied with this first decision," they said in a joint statement issued on Wednesday after the court's decision.

L'Express has alleged that Hernu was paid for supplying general information on French politics and other subjects such as the size of the French army fighting rebels in Algeria, and the address of U.S. secret services in Paris.

L'Express said the French DST counter-intelligence service had informed the late president Francois Mitterrand, Hernu's political patron, in 1992 after it received a dossier from east European spy services.
It said the DST had been unable to verify the charges and Mitterrand had ordered the reports kept secret, arguing that Hernu was dead and could not defend himself.

In their statement, the sons demanded a meeting with Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre or the DST chief to clear up any doubt about the documents. They also called for the ministry to publish documents it had relating to the issue.
